races.name: ABP Ports Of Grimsby & Immingham Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
GP Shipping Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Won last two starts on Good ground including over 2m6f, suggesting this longer trip and surface suit well; hold-up style is natural but needs something to aim at — a slowly run race in front is the enemy, though the fading-in-finish flag is a genuine concern at this distance.

runners_data.name: Braganza Bay
runners_data.note: The key pace influence — sole confirmed front-runner who can set fractions to suit himself on 43 days off; STYLE_FIT tag is noted as he is mapped as prominent rather than a true lone leader, though his record of four wins on Good ground reinforces his chance if left uncontested.

runners_data.name: Reforme
runners_data.note: Form string ends in two pull-ups (P) which cannot be ignored; trainer Gretton has no winners from two in the last 14 days and 0W2P on similar going does not inspire confidence, though three placed efforts on Good ground keep a sliver of hope alive.

runners_data.name: Cinderello
runners_data.note: Three wins from five runs, all on Good ground, and the last two over distances close to today's 2m7f — Alex Hales's runner is the most dangerous hold-up-to-prominent type if Hogan elects to press the leader rather than settle in behind.

runners_data.name: Jungle Wood
runners_data.note: Amateur claimer Miss Lily Bradstock takes 7lbs off but Jungle Wood has gone winless in five runs since a 2m3f win; hold-up style is natural and the 2m6f Good-ground fifth last time shows the trip is fine, but trainer has no recent runners to assess form on.

runners_data.name: Klervia
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position by the crowd of closers in this field — Fergal O'Brien's runner has form on Good ground and a 3lb claimer in the saddle, but stepping up markedly in trip from recent 2m runs is an untested factor and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Moro Rock
runners_data.note: Returned a flat fifth last time out on 70 days' absence and will need to be closer to the pace than his natural hold-up instincts allow; genuine hold-up type forced into a midfield role here, and Sara Ender's 0W4P 14-day record adds no confidence — the Good-going record (1W, 6P) shows he handles it at least.

runners_data.name: Matoury
runners_data.note: Mike Sowersby has 0W2P in the last 14 days and Matoury's last four runs include a pull-up; a true hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield given the depth of closers in this field, and while a recent third on Good ground is encouraging, the combination of trip concerns (mostly run at 2m) and jockey claim is uncertain.

runners_data.name: Time Was
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby has 0W21 in the past fortnight which is a stark trainer statistic; history is almost entirely at 2m on Soft ground (four of last five), and this 2m7f Good-ground assignment represents a significant step up in both trip and going — mapped to midfield though a natural rear-of-field runner.

runners_data.name: Lady Fortune
runners_data.note: Won last time on Good over 2m which is a confidence-booster, but six furlongs shorter than today's trip is a substantial query; hold-up style is her natural mode and she has been placed to midfield because of the cluster of closers — McPherson and Killahena's yard has 1W7 in the last 14 days, suggesting some form in the team.

races.paceDynamic: Braganza Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 2m7f handicap hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, Sam Twiston-Davies should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Market Rasen. That lone-pace scenario suits a prominent racer able to dictate tempo and conserve energy for the final climb, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to generate the momentum needed to reel him in late. The field is unusually hold-up heavy — Moro Rock, Matoury, Klervia, Time Was and Lady Fortune are all true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because the genuine rear-of-field positions are overcrowded; Cinderello is the only other horse capable of racing prominently and applying any pressure to the leader. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead runners who can control fractions, with hold-up profiles at a structural disadvantage given the lack of pressure to create a true end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Braganza Bay Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Braganza Bay leads uncontested and sets a measured pace that turns this into a test of jumping and jumping rhythm rather than raw stamina.
scenarios.body: If Braganza Bay leads uncontested and sets a measured pace that turns this into a test of jumping and jumping rhythm rather than raw stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Cinderello Pressures Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Cinderello tracks Braganza Bay prominently, puts him under pressure from three out and forces a true stamina test.
scenarios.body: If Cinderello tracks Braganza Bay prominently, puts him under pressure from three out and forces a true stamina test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If Braganza Bay's controlled pace paradoxically creates a falsely run contest and a cluster of hold-up horses closes powerfully in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Braganza Bay's controlled pace paradoxically creates a falsely run contest and a cluster of hold-up horses closes powerfully in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers or a ragged pace causes multiple runners to lose positions or pull up, fundamentally altering the complexion mid-race.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors, fallers or a ragged pace causes multiple runners to lose positions or pull up, fundamentally altering the complexion mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Braganza Bay — if Sam Twiston-Davies is allowed to bowl along unchallenged from flag to finish, the race may be over as a contest before the home straight; watch whether Cinderello or any other prominent type moves up to pressure him at halfway.

Muskerry Rock — flagged as fading in the finish, which is a serious concern in a 2m7f on Good ground if the pace is even moderate; watch whether Harry Skelton settles him close enough to avoid a long run to the line.

Time Was and Lady Fortune — both true hold-up horses racing significantly further than their recent form trips and on much better ground than their last five runs suggest they like; a pace mismatch here could leave both trailing irreversibly from the home turn.

Klervia, Moro Rock, Matoury — three genuine hold-up types all effectively competing for the same tactical position in the back half of the field; congestion approaching the final bend could cause interference or one of them being shuffled back at a critical moment.

Jungle Wood — amateur jockey Miss Bradstock (7lb claim) aboard a horse with a headgear flag (p); watch whether the headgear change lifts his early position, as his hold-up style combined with the amateur ride makes positional management at Market Rasen's turns a factor.

races.name: Dan Shipping Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Wings On Wheels
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner freshened up on just 8 days' turnaround, wearing hood and tongue strap, with two places from seven on similar Good ground; she is the lone pace-setter here and will control the tempo entirely, but her STYLE_FIT tag signals she is racing slightly out of her natural role and her chance is best assessed against how well she can actually hold that advantage jumping the final fences.|

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's yard is in red-hot form at 9/22 over the last 14 days, and Harry Skelton partnering a horse that has won and placed twice over this course-and-distance trip on Good ground is a significant angle; a genuine hold-up horse who will settle near the rear, his recent win over 21f on Good ground is directly relevant and he carries the stable confidence that counts.|

runners_data.name: Arctic Saint
runners_data.note: Deborah Cole's runner returns after a 70-day absence — that layoff is worth monitoring — but he has a strong profile of placing on Good ground with two from thirteen recorded over similar terrain; a natural hold-up horse who will race from the rear, the step up to 2m3f is well within his comfort zone and James Bowen riding for the in-form Cole yard adds a tactical edge.|

runners_data.name: Shes All Pride
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride on this OR 78 mare who has shown three places from seven Good-ground runs including a third at 22f; her natural inclination is to race from behind, though the hold-up-heavy field means she is likely to find herself in a more prominent position than she'd ideally want — that positional compromise is a mild negative against her true style.|

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Veteran 12-year-old for Micky Hammond, dropping to OR 71 with Brian Hughes in the saddle, and the data across 15 similar-going runs — five places including a win — shows a horse that is reliably consistent on Good ground; he is a genuine hold-up type who may find himself racing closer to the pace than he prefers given how many rear-runners are in this field, though his experience should help him handle the congestion.|

runners_data.name: Chateau Du Lys
runners_data.note: Tom Gretton's gelding comes in on a career-low OR 65 with claimer William Maggs taking a 3lb claim, and three places from ten Good-ground runs suggest the surface is no issue; like Getaway Jewel and Shes All Pride, he wants to race from the back but the hold-up-heavy field will likely push him closer to the pace — low weight and a fresh 19-day break are the positives, the positional squeeze is the concern.|

races.paceDynamic: Wings On Wheels is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner handicap chase over 2m3f on Good ground at Market Rasen, and with no natural challenger for the lead, she is set to dictate a controlled, uncrowded gallop from the front. Behind her, Thickthorn Tom and Arctic Saint are genuine hold-up horses who will track from the rear, while Shes All Pride, Getaway Jewel, and Chateau Du Lys are all true hold-up types that the map has pushed into midfield slots simply because the rear is oversubscribed — in reality, all three will want to race further back than their mapped positions suggest. The result is a race where Wings On Wheels controls the tempo alone, setting a sustainable pace that risks flattening into a test of jumping accuracy and staying power rather than a lung-bursting finish. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with strong finishes on Good ground, particularly those who can travel well off the bridle and quicken over the final two fences — Thickthorn Tom and Arctic Saint are best placed to exploit that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wings On Wheels Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Wings On Wheels bowls along unchallenged at a steady-to-fair pace and the hold-up brigade fail to close down the advantage turning in.
scenarios.body: If Wings On Wheels bowls along unchallenged at a steady-to-fair pace and the hold-up brigade fail to close down the advantage turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady early and the hold-up horses travel fluently to deliver coordinated late challenges from two out.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady early and the hold-up horses travel fluently to deliver coordinated late challenges from two out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaotic Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the field's true hold-up horses all commit to forward positions early, creating a messy, contested pace that fractures the race shape mid-contest.
scenarios.body: If the field's true hold-up horses all commit to forward positions early, creating a messy, contested pace that fractures the race shape mid-contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely at the top of the straight and a low-weighted, well-ridden runner at big odds exploits a gap that opens between the leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely at the top of the straight and a low-weighted, well-ridden runner at big odds exploits a gap that opens between the leaders.

watchPoints.text: Watch Wings On Wheels's jumping under Charlie Todd — if she gets away cleanly at the first two fences and establishes a clear lead with no front-running rival to challenge her, she could dictate the entire race from an uncontested position and prove very difficult to reel in.

Monitor Thickthorn Tom's position in the early stages — Harry Skelton may elect to sit closer than usual given the steady likely pace, and if he travels smoothly in second or third turning for home he becomes the primary danger to Wings On Wheels off the front.

The cluster of true hold-up horses — Shes All Pride, Getaway Jewel, and Chateau Du Lys — all want the same rear ground, and a scrappy, jostling early passage on the first circuit at Market Rasen's tight track could compromise their runs before the race even develops properly.

Arctic Saint's 70-day absence is a flag worth watching at the start — if he breaks sluggishly or settles awkwardly in the early stages, Deborah Cole will need him to warm into the race, which is manageable over this trip on Good ground but warrants attention before committing.

The Good going is consistent across every Market Rasen race today, meaning no unexpected surface variation; however, the compact, flat-turning nature of the track means any horse that loses momentum mid-race through a jumping error at a far-side fence will struggle to recover against a leader already in full stride.

races.name: Global Shipping Services Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hello Sweety
runners_data.note: Five-year-old in excellent form (won last two, including a course win over 2m at Market Rasen on Good), Stuart Edmunds has a quiet 14-day record (0/1) but the horse's recent profile is strong; natural hold-up racer who will need Beorma to be caught, but the 19-day turnaround looks sharp and she is the most obvious beneficiary if the pace softens in the straight.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, unbeaten in six starts including multiple wins at today's trip and going, and Dan Skelton's yard is firing at 50% over the past 14 days (12/24); ran seven days ago so freshness bears monitoring, but the style fit for this race shape is overwhelming and she requires no help from the field to dictate.

runners_data.name: The Secret Pearl
runners_data.note: Alex Hales runner has been placing consistently in similar distances and going but her last six runs include a pull-up and several mid-division finishes; headgear (tongue-strap, pads) suggests connections are trying to sharpen her, and while she handles Good ground she will need the pace to collapse late to land a blow from her natural position at the back.

runners_data.name: Miracles Do Happen
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good ground last time out — that form is highly relevant — but the reality here is that she races in a hold-up style that the current race shape does not favour, forced to show from further back than she would ideally like; Tom Lacey's 14-day strike rate (0/8) adds caution, though the raw form demands respect.

runners_data.name: Assorda
runners_data.note: John Wainwright's six-year-old has been a consistent mid-to-rear finisher across her last five starts, never troubling the winner; although she handles Good ground and the trip, her recent string of fifth and sixth places (P66-56) suggests she is not going up in the handicap for a reason, and her chances hinge entirely on everything else under-performing.

runners_data.name: Kottayam
runners_data.note: Two pull-ups and a 10th on her most recent visible form readings, and she hasn't run for 58 days — fitness is the first question; a natural hold-up racer whose best recent effort (2nd over 2m Good) came some time ago, and the combination of layoff, inconsistent jumping and this race shape make her difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Miss Friday Lions
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies has shown 1/19 over 14 days so trainer form is modest; this five-year-old ran a creditable third at Market Rasen on Good last time over 2m1f and is clearly suited by the track, but she races from the rear by inclination and the headgear (hood) suggests jumping or focus issues that could prove costly.

runners_data.name: Little Soiree
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old at OR 78 carrying the minimum weight but her last six runs include two pull-ups and a string of mid-pack finishes; Olly Williams is 0/3 in the 14-day window and the horse's best form is on Soft ground, making the Good surface here a further query on top of her modest recent profile.

races.paceDynamic: Beorma is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner mares' handicap hurdle over 2m½f on Good ground at Market Rasen, and with Harry Skelton aboard a horse boasting a perfect six-from-six career record, she will stride into the lead from the outset and control a measured, sustainable tempo. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Hello Sweety, The Secret Pearl, Miracles Do Happen, Assorda, Kottayam, Miss Friday Lions and Little Soiree all prefer to race from off the pace — meaning Beorma will dictate in total isolation with no pressure whatsoever. This creates a genuinely uncontested, front-runner-favours shape: Beorma can bowl along at her own rhythm, conserve energy over her hurdles and kick again turning for home before the closers have a chance to organise their challenge. The race shape strongly favours Beorma herself and those closest to her early on, with true hold-up horses disadvantaged by the probability that Beorma builds a commanding, untroubled lead that may prove impossible to peg back from off a slow, uncontested gallop. Several hold-up horses — Miracles Do Happen, Assorda, Kottayam, Miss Friday Lions and Little Soiree — are mapped to midfield only because the field contains far more horses wanting the rear than the pace map can physically show there; Beorma and, to a lesser extent, Hello Sweety are likeliest to actually secure the forward positions in practice.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beorma Bowls Clear Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma leads throughout at a comfortable gallop and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Beorma leads throughout at a comfortable gallop and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Peg Back Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just slow enough to bunch the field and a well-timed hold-up horse delivers a decisive late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves just slow enough to bunch the field and a well-timed hold-up horse delivers a decisive late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma is tracked closely by a challenger who refuses to concede the pace and quickens past her at the last.
scenarios.body: If Beorma is tracked closely by a challenger who refuses to concede the pace and quickens past her at the last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses after the last and a true back-marker produces a sustained run from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses after the last and a true back-marker produces a sustained run from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Beorma (Harry Skelton) jumping fluently at the first two hurdles — if she skips clear cleanly she will be almost impossible to catch given the uncontested pace she will set.
Hello Sweety needs to be in a forward position turning out of the back straight; if she gets shuffled back behind the midfield cluster she may find the winning post comes too soon.

Miracles Do Happen holds the strongest recent form in the field (won here last time) but her hold-up style is structurally disadvantaged in this shape — watch whether Gavin Sheehan tries to push her up earlier than usual.
Kottayam has not run for 58 days and has a history of pulling up — monitor her jumping closely in the early stages as any mistake or refusal will shape the complexion of the race behind Beorma.

The pace map is almost entirely hold-up horses behind one front-runner; if Beorma meets a hurdle wrong and loses momentum mid-race, the entire field will bunch rapidly and the race dynamic could flip dramatically in the straight.

races.name: Associated British Ports "Summer Plate Trial" Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mahons Glory
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran rated 139 who has won on soft but whose recent form over 2m2f–2m6f on good shows solid consistency (nine places from 15 similar-going runs); Lee Edwards partners him for Dylan Cunha's small yard (T14: 1/19), and while he is a natural pace-setter who should lead comfortably, his age and a 55-day absence are mild concerns if the finish becomes a sprint.

runners_data.name: Bhaloo
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's eight-year-old arrives in excellent nick (T14: 5/20), which is the standout trainer-form angle in this field; last seen finishing second at Goodwood over 2m4f on good and has placed three times from nine runs on similar ground, suggesting conditions are ideal and a well-supported prominent position should translate directly into a competitive finish.

runners_data.name: Genois
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for Jonjo & A J O'Neill (T14: 1/23) on a horse who has been remarkably consistent in 2025 — three wins and a second from his last five, including victories on soft and a second on good over 2m; the step up to 2m5½f is a question mark given all his recent runs have been around 2m, but his jumping prowess and high cruising speed make him dangerous if the trip is within range.

runners_data.name: Bleu d'Enfer
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's eight-year-old is the only genuine hold-up horse in the field and wears a tongue-piece, with Theo Gillard (T14: 1/14) likely to settle him well off the pace; his best recent form shows two seconds over 2m on good ground, but his chance is entirely contingent on a genuinely run race creating enough momentum for a late challenge — the controlled pace expected here is a tactical headwind.

runners_data.name: Seaview Rock
runners_data.note: Charles & Adam Pogson's lightly-weighted six-year-old (OR 117, 146lbs) is the youngest horse in the race and showed real ability winning at Huntingdon in heavy and placing twice on good; naturally a prominent racer, he is likely to find himself crowded out of his preferred early position given the number of similar types in this field, and Robert Dunne will need to adapt his ride if he cannot slot in where he wants.

runners_data.name: Gateau De Miel
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's 10-year-old comes here fresh off a 21f good-ground win 20 days ago (T14: 1/25), wearing a tongue-piece, and has the best recent form of the three horses pushed out of their natural prominent position; Tom Broughton takes a 3lb claiming allowance which partially offsets his weight, but finding himself forced to race further back than ideal against his instincts remains the key obstacle to a repeat win.

runners_data.name: Ostend
runners_data.note: Alastair Ralph's eight-year-old (T14: 0/7) has been off 69 days — the longest absence in the field — and his form figures of P/334 suggest he has not recaptured his best since winning on good going; a genuine front-runner by nature, he is the third horse displaced from his preferred prominent role and faces the double challenge of freshness concerns and racing in a position that will not suit his jumping style.

races.paceDynamic: Mahons Glory is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a field of seven, is likely to control this race from the outset at a sustainable gallop on good ground over 2m5½f — conditions that suit a patient, rhythm-based approach rather than a war of attrition. Bhaloo, Genois and the redistributed trio of Seaview Rock, Gateau De Miel and Ostend are all naturally prominent types, meaning there is significant competition for early position behind Mahons Glory, but only two or three horses can realistically sit in the front rank and the others will be shuffled back against their instincts. Bleu d'Enfer is the sole genuine hold-up horse and will be ridden patiently by Theo Gillard, arriving late if the pace is strong enough to create a genuine target. This race shape — one uncontested leader setting a controlled tempo with a congested chase pack behind — strongly favours prominent or close-tracking horses who get their natural position early, as the lack of genuine pressure from Mahons Glory means the race will not truly string out, and a late surge from a true hold-up position is less likely to be rewarded. The field holds more naturally prominent types than can all secure that position: Bhaloo and Genois, with their higher ratings and top yards, are best placed to hold prominent ground, while Seaview Rock, Gateau De Miel and Ostend are most likely to find themselves racing out of their preferred role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Mahons Glory leads uncontested at a measured gallop and the chasing pack burns energy disputing second.
scenarios.body: If Mahons Glory leads uncontested at a measured gallop and the chasing pack burns energy disputing second.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Increases Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group sends pace sharply upward in the middle section, testing stamina and setting up a late finish.
scenarios.body: If the congested prominent group sends pace sharply upward in the middle section, testing stamina and setting up a late finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Mahons Glory's controlled pace proves impossible to reel in and the chasers fail to close the gap when it matters.
scenarios.body: If Mahons Glory's controlled pace proves impossible to reel in and the chasers fail to close the gap when it matters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Seaview Rock, Gateau De Miel or Ostend manage to secure prominent positions despite the overcrowded pace map and produce career-best efforts.
scenarios.body: If Seaview Rock, Gateau De Miel or Ostend manage to secure prominent positions despite the overcrowded pace map and produce career-best efforts.

watchPoints.text: Bhaloo's trainer Nicky Henderson has sent out five winners from 20 runners in the last 14 days — the hottest yard in this race — and if James Bowen slots him directly behind Mahons Glory, he may be able to dictate terms on his own from that position.

Watch for early jostling between Seaview Rock, Gateau De Miel and Ostend in the first half-mile as three naturally prominent types compete for only one or two available tracking positions — any scrimmaging or interference here could compromise more than one runner's chance.

Genois has not run beyond 2m1f in any of his last five outings; Harry Cobden will need to judge the pace carefully in the final mile, as the 2m5½f trip is an unproven stamina test and if he strikes the front too soon he may idle or empty late.

Mahons Glory has not won since a soft-ground success at Ffos Las and all five of his career wins have come on soft or heavy going — today's good ground is within range of his OK tag but worth monitoring in the context of whether he can hold on from the front if Bhaloo or Genois attack him turning in.

Bleu d'Enfer's tongue-piece is on for the first time based on headgear flag; if it sharpens his jumping and Gillard produces him late on the inner, he becomes a dark-horse closer — but only if the pace shape delivers a genuinely strong gallop, which a single uncontested front-runner is unlikely to provide.

races.name: ABP Ports Of Hull & Goole Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tuba
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who got off the mark over C&D last time (19 days ago) and should secure a comfortable, uncontested lead; STYLE_FIT flag suggests she is not ideally profiled for prominent racing but here she is the pace — the concern is whether she can maintain it over this 2m4½f trip at the top weight of 168lbs.

runners_data.name: Vivid Pink
runners_data.note: Returned from a 229-day break with a creditable run and has an excellent Good-ground record (8/11 similar going), making her one of the better-placed prominent types to track Tuba and challenge late; Alan King's 1/16 14-day strike rate is positive and Tom Bellamy is an accomplished partner over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Lone Star
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse for Philip Kirby who has run well on Good ground multiple times (12/15 sim-going) and handles this sort of trip; 22 days since last run is fine but he is a 9-year-old who will need significant pace collapse to pick up enough ground from the rear.

runners_data.name: Midnight Pass
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Emma Lavelle who has been placed on Good ground in all eight similar-going starts (0W3P) yet to win on this surface; James Bowen can claim and the horse is consistent without being a standout — likely to travel well but may lack the finishing kick to pass the best.

runners_data.name: Gms Prince
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran with Good-ground form and an honest record, likely to track prominently as usual; his OR of 88 leaves him competitive but his age and recent consistency (placed without winning) suggest he fills a frame role rather than a winning one.

runners_data.name: Bunker Bay
runners_data.note: Back just 7 days after winning last week (OR 88), this is a fit horse in the best recent form in the race with two wins on Good ground; apprentice Joshua Thompson (5) rides, which adds a risk element, but the form figures of 328-11 speak loudly and Good going clearly suits.

runners_data.name: Mancero
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 4-year-old, lightest in the race at 151lbs with Jack Tudor aboard; a winner over 20f on Good ground last time (22 days ago) and has been remarkably consistent, making him a prominent type with genuine claims if he handles the step up to 20f+ on this track.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse for the small Sowersby yard (0/6 T14) who has struggled to place recently (form /36-50) and whose best form is on distances shorter than today's 2m4½f; likely to race at the rear and faces a stiff ask to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Onehundredneighty
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's 6-year-old prefers to come from off the pace but has been squeezed into a midfield map position by the volume of hold-up types in this field; his Good-ground best figures (2/8 sim-going without a win) and the fact he won't get his ideal position significantly limit his chance.

runners_data.name: Earlofbrackenstown
runners_data.note: Carries a finish-fade flag and a form string of PP0P-P, suggesting completion rather than competition has been the recent theme; though naturally a hold-up performer, the horse ends up mapped ahead of its true preference and its record on Good ground (7/11 sim-going, 0W) offers no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Bargain Hunter
runners_data.note: Absent 93 days and returning for the small Jeffreys yard (0/1 T14); the form figures of 57890- on Good ground are uniformly poor and, while the horse is a genuine hold-up type, it cannot naturally operate from the back in this shape and the sharp fitness doubt compounds an already difficult task.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner so has no bearing on race shape; noted for record purposes only — had headgear (visor) and a decent Good-ground profile (12/15 sim-going, 2W5P) but does not factor in the tactical analysis.

races.paceDynamic: Tuba is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to push for the lead from the outset, she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Market Rasen's easy-turning track over 2m4½f on Good ground. Vivid Pink, Midnight Pass, Gms Prince and Mancero are all prominent-racing types who will contest the early positions behind Tuba, creating a compact, bunched group through the early stages rather than a strung-out affair. Bunker Bay is the most potent recent form-horse in the field and, although a natural hold-up performer, has won twice on Good ground at this level and will be produced as late as his apprentice rider dares. The race shape — one honest front-runner setting a fair but uncontested gallop — overwhelmingly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and pick it up in the straight, with hold-up horses needing everything to go perfectly against a well-strung-out field; notably, Onehundredneighty, Earlofbrackenstown and Bargain Hunter are genuine hold-up types redistributed into the midfield map because the true rear of the field is more congested than the pace positions, meaning they are unlikely to travel in their preferred spots or deliver their finishing kicks as cleanly as their styles demand.

watchPoints.text: Bunker Bay has won back-to-back and is the most in-form horse in the field — watch whether apprentice Joshua Thompson (5) can hold him up sufficiently to produce his run at the right moment, as any positional error in a compact bunch behind Tuba could cost him.

Tuba is carrying top weight (168lbs) as the race's only front-runner; if she sets too strong a pace to dominate, she may tire dramatically at the last hurdle, which would benefit whoever is closest behind — watch Vivid Pink and Mancero's positioning at halfway.

Mancero is only 4 years old and today steps up modestly in trip at a track he hasn't visited before; if he fails to travel smoothly around Market Rasen's tight bends, Jack Tudor may find him running flat in the closing stages despite his low weight.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Onehundredneighty, Earlofbrackenstown, Bargain Hunter) are all unlikely to get their natural position — watch early for any signs of them being pushed wider or forward than ideal, as it will expose the limits of their finishing kicks.

Vivid Pink returns from 229 days off; watch her behaviour in the paddock and her jumping at the first two hurdles, as a rusty jumper coming back from a long layoff could lose her prominent position quickly in a field this competitive.
